about: CPCM's published measurements; the release summary's CPCM entries are built from it
build: Andrey at commit 9f36092dc, CPCM as merged into the 0.19.0 release branch (the smoothing criterion of the exponential, Pareto, and Poisson fits); the rows whose families that change does not touch (Table 1's gamma with fixed shape and misspecified families, and the graphs G1, G2 and the lambda = 1 arms, Gaussian fixed scale throughout) ran on commit 68170983b of the 0.18.0 line, whose CPCM code is the same for those families. The release branch's CPCM code is the measured build's. On Table 2's POISg and PARg, both data sources, CPCM, the authors' code on the authors' generator's tables, and loci, anm and pnl ran in one job on one node, on commit 9f36092dc; CPCM's decisions there equal those of its earlier run on the Appendix B.3 tables

comparators.CPCM authors' R code: CPCM_graph_estimate from the code published with the paper (commit 2ada90e), sourced unmodified, with R 4.6.1, mgcv 1.9.5, dHSIC 2.2, gamlss 5.5.5 and bnlearn 5.2.1; the same family or family collection as Andrey's arm, lambda as Andrey's, quiet = TRUE, set.seed(seed) before each call
comparators.frontier, pairs: andrey.loci, andrey.anm, andrey.pnl at their defaults
comparators.frontier, graphs: andrey.resit, andrey.direct_lingam, andrey.ica_lingam, andrey.pc (fisherz and kci), andrey.ges, andrey.cam, andrey.score_matching, andrey.nogam at their defaults

verdict_rule: per cell (setup, family arm, size): D = error(Andrey) - error(reference) per dataset, on the datasets both fitted (pairs: 1 for the reversed forced direction; graphs: SHD, and the authors' SID beside it, a graph worse on either being worse); worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; 10,000 resamples, default_rng(0). Pairs: 100 per cell, graphs: 20. A row worse on its first seeds was rerun on fresh seeds, and holds that rerun as replication; every other pair row with fresh seeds holds them as fresh. Fresh graph rows have no reference arm: Andrey's errors and floors only. result is the published verdict, better or worse only where the fresh seeds agree, a tie otherwise. The floor field is Andrey's and the reference's error minus the empty answer's; the lane file also gives the floor of the better of the coin flip and the cell's majority direction (pairs) or the empty and the base-rate graph (graphs). Rows of Table 1's misspecified families, the other family arm on LS, LS-s and MN-U, Table 2's PARg (out_of_claim gives the reason), and the edge penalty 1 are out of claim, reported
seeds_note: pairs: first seeds 0-99, fresh seeds 100-199; Table 2: the first seeds are the 100 pairs of each of the five Tagasovska et al. (2020) files the paper takes them from, and the fresh seeds 100 pairs drawn by those files' generator, unmodified, under another seed. That generator at the published commit reproduces the MN-U file exactly and the AN file's causes and directions, but not the AN-s, LS and LS-s files, which match the fresh draws on summary statistics only (the cause's and the effect's spread, kurtosis). POISg and PARg have no published data and were drawn as the paper's Appendix B.3 describes them, under the pair seeds 0-99 and 100-199: the cause N(0, sqrt 2) (standard deviation sqrt 2), theta(x) = f(x) - min f + 0.5 with f a zero-mean Gaussian process with a squared-exponential kernel, sigma 1 and length 0.2, on a grid spanning the cause, and the effect Poisson with mean theta or Pareto of scale 1 and shape theta, the pair's order swapped on a coin. Both sets were also drawn by the authors' own generator (CPCM_generative_model in Simulations/Simulations2/Data generators.R, commit 2ada90e, sourced unmodified with EnvStats 3.1.0, 100 pairs of 1,000 rows per set under set.seed(0), the seed of the authors' simulation script, for the first seeds and set.seed(2026) for the fresh seeds), the pair's order swapped on a coin drawn outside R's stream; that generator differs from the description in three ways: it reads theta from a grid of 201 points that starts at 0, so theta is a step function, constant for causes below 0, and it draws the Pareto effect with EnvStats' rpareto(1, theta, 1), whose arguments are the location and the shape, which gives scale theta and shape 1. Its tables are not the authors' own draws, since their script runs the methods between draws; graphs: first seeds 0-19, fresh seeds 20-39
fit_protocol: each fit in a long-lived worker on one core with one BLAS thread, one timed fit, a cap of 1,800 s per fit (3,600 s for the reference at 8 variables); no fit timed out; the reference's errors are counted and never scored, and each cell is paired on the datasets both finished; times are wall seconds of the fit inside the worker

regimes.cpcm_table1_exponential: the CPCM paper's Table 1 pairs: X1 ~ N(2, 1) on x > 0, X2 given X1 exponential with rate theta(X1), 1,000 rows, fitted with the exponential family
regimes.cpcm_table1_gamma_fixed_shape: the CPCM paper's Table 1 pairs: X1 ~ N(2, 1) on x > 0, X2 given X1 exponential with rate theta(X1), 1,000 rows, fitted with the gamma_fixed_shape family
regimes.cpcm_table1_pareto: the CPCM paper's Table 1 pairs: X1 ~ N(2, 1) on x > 0, X2 given X1 exponential with rate theta(X1), 1,000 rows, fitted with the pareto family
regimes.cpcm_table1_gamma: the CPCM paper's Table 1 pairs: X1 ~ N(2, 1) on x > 0, X2 given X1 exponential with rate theta(X1), 1,000 rows, fitted with the gamma family
regimes.cpcm_table1_gumbel: the CPCM paper's Table 1 pairs: X1 ~ N(2, 1) on x > 0, X2 given X1 exponential with rate theta(X1), 1,000 rows, fitted with the gumbel family
regimes.cpcm_table1_gumbel_fixed_scale: the CPCM paper's Table 1 pairs: X1 ~ N(2, 1) on x > 0, X2 given X1 exponential with rate theta(X1), 1,000 rows, fitted with the gumbel_fixed_scale family
regimes.cpcm_table1_gaussian: the CPCM paper's Table 1 pairs: X1 ~ N(2, 1) on x > 0, X2 given X1 exponential with rate theta(X1), 1,000 rows, fitted with the gaussian family
regimes.cpcm_table1_gaussian_fixed_scale: the CPCM paper's Table 1 pairs: X1 ~ N(2, 1) on x > 0, X2 given X1 exponential with rate theta(X1), 1,000 rows, fitted with the gaussian_fixed_scale family
regimes.cpcm_table2: the CPCM paper's Table 2 pairs, 1,000 rows: the five synthetic sets of Tagasovska et al. (2020) and the paper's Poisson and Pareto setups, each drawn as its Appendix B.3 describes and by the authors' generator, with the family the paper's rule picks from each column's support, or the Gaussian location-scale family on the location-scale and multiplicative sets
regimes.cpcm_table2_other_arm: the CPCM paper's Table 2 pairs, each fitted with the other family arm: the fixed-scale Gaussian family given on AN and AN-s, the support rule's family on LS, LS-s and MN-U
regimes.cpcm_pareto16: the CPCM paper's model (16): X2 given X1 Pareto with theta(x) = x^gamma log x + 1, gamma 1 or 2, 500 to 2,000 rows
regimes.cpcm_graph_paper: the CPCM paper's Section 6.4 graphs: random DAGs of 5 variables, 1,000 rows, linear, additive-noise, exponential CPCM, and mixed exponential and Gaussian CPCM variables, with the families the paper's rule picks from each column's support
regimes.cpcm_graph_paper_lambda1: as cpcm_graph_paper, with an edge penalty of 1, the default of the authors' scripts
regimes.cpcm_graph_greedy: the CPCM paper's Appendix B.1.1 graphs: exponential CPCM variables on random DAGs of 4, 6 and 8 variables, 1,000 rows, the families from the support rule

parity.build: Andrey at commit 9f36092dc, CPCM as merged into the 0.19.0 release branch (the smoothing criterion of the exponential, Pareto, and Poisson fits); the rows whose families that change does not touch (Table 1's gamma with fixed shape and misspecified families, and the graphs G1, G2 and the lambda = 1 arms, Gaussian fixed scale throughout) ran on commit 68170983b of the 0.18.0 line, whose CPCM code is the same for those families. The release branch's CPCM code is the measured build's. On Table 2's POISg and PARg, both data sources, CPCM, the authors' code on the authors' generator's tables, and loci, anm and pnl ran in one job on one node, on commit 9f36092dc; CPCM's decisions there equal those of its earlier run on the Appendix B.3 tables

conservative_estimate.about: model (16) at 500 rows, the conservative estimate at alpha 0.05 read from one forced fit's p-values: the share of pairs with X1 -> X2, X2 -> X1, no edge with the columns independent (empty), both directions plausible (both), and neither; the claimed outcome is X1 -> X2 for gamma > 0 and no orientation (empty, both, or neither) for gamma <= 0, fixed before the results; parity pairs the misses of the claimed outcome, Andrey minus the reference, paired bootstrap 95% interval; at gamma 0, whose claim in the paper is both directions plausible, parity_both_only pairs the misses of that outcome alone, and the result at gamma 0 is read from it; Table 4 is the paper's row. The conservative estimate under the Pareto family is out of the supported claim: at gamma 0 Andrey finds both directions plausible less often than the reference on both seed sets (see gaps.pareto_basis)

frontier.about: beside other Andrey methods on the same datasets: a comparator dominates CPCM when its paired error interval lies below CPCM's (accuracy for pairs, SID for graphs) and its paired mean log-seconds ratio interval lies below 0, with seconds paired only where both fits ran on the same node; CPCM's arm is the claimed one. pc returns a CPDAG, which the authors' SID scores with its undirected edges read both ways

gaps.pareto_basis: On model (16), Andrey's p-value of one direction falls far below the reference's on some pairs (16 of 400 fits at gamma 0, 500 rows), 14 of them where the covariate's largest value is more than 844 times its median, the top tenth of the pairs, where it happens on 35% of fits against 0-2.5% elsewhere. At gamma 0 the conservative estimate finds both directions plausible, the paper's claim there, less often than the reference on both seed sets (parity_both_only: +0.09 [+0.04, +0.15] first, +0.07 [+0.02, +0.13] fresh), so the conservative estimate under the Pareto family is out of the supported claim; pooled as no orientation (empty, both, or neither), the measure fixed before the runs, the misses are +0.06 [-0.01, +0.13] first and +0.08 [+0.02, +0.14] fresh, because Andrey's extra "neither" results count as hits there. At gamma 2 and 2,000 rows the forced direction is wrong on 8 of 200 pairs against 1. Ranked cause: the rank-10 thin plate spline basis on a covariate with extreme values, located, not yet traced to a difference from the authors' basis (mgcv's tp). Fix plan: compare Andrey's basis, penalty and fitted parameters with mgcv's on the pairs where the p-value collapses, follow the authors' construction where they differ, and rerun model (16)
gaps.pareto_authors_generator: On PARg drawn by the authors' generator (Pareto effects of scale theta and shape 1), the forced direction is right on 0.38 of the first seeds' pairs in both implementations and on 0.47 and 0.46 of the fresh ones, no better than a coin flip, so Table 2's PARg setup is out of the supported claim on both data sources. Ranked causes: (1) the family; the support rule gives the effect the exponential family (167 of 200 pairs) or the Pareto family of scale 1 (33), neither of which holds a Pareto of varying scale and shape 1. The authors' code with the paper's sequential choice of the family, which Andrey does not implement, was right on 0.66 of the pairs on both seed sets (cause evidence, not a measured arm). (2) The data: theta is constant for causes below 0, about half of the rows, and the effect's mean is infinite; no comparator was right on more than 0.44 of the pairs. Fix plan: implement the paper's sequential choice of the family, rerun PARg on both data sources against the authors' code with the same choice, and judge it again
gaps.mn_u_fresh: On the fresh MN-U draws, loci named the true direction more often (0.98 against 0.84) and faster; on the shipped files it did not (0.98 against 0.96)
gaps.support_rule_on_location_scale: On LS, LS-s and MN-U the support rule picks the fixed-scale Gaussian family, an additive-noise model, in both implementations; there the forced direction is right on 0.58, 0.03 and 0.00 of the shipped pairs. The paper's sequential choice of the family is not implemented
